title: Bootcamp accelerator: SDK roadtrip notes and quickstart checklist
content:
Purpose:
A compact field guide for the 2-day SDK bootcamp we run for new integrators and internal devs. Focus: remove friction, validate telemetry, and hand a working sample app in under 90 minutes. Treat as a living sprint artifact — lightweight, opinionated, and intentionally rough.

Audience:
- New hires on devex and solutions teams
- Customer engineers doing first integration
- PMs and SEs who need a reproducible demo path

Core goals (success criteria for a bootcamp run):
1) Participant checks out example repo and runs full demo with local emulated env in <= 90 minutes.
2) Sample app makes 3 different Redwood API calls (generate, chat, embedding) and logs telemetry to Sentry/Datadog.
3) Participants can toggle local failover to sidecar and observe fallback behavior.
4) Post-run survey average helpfulness >= 4/5 and at least 80% can reproduce demo after 24h.

Sprint checklist (minimal viable runbook):
- Pre-reqs email (48h before): node/python runtime, Git, Docker, access token (ephemeral). Link to quick token exchange: /internal/token-ops.
- Pre-provisioned workspace: Vagrant-lite / devcontainer with all env variables stubbed.
- Starter repo: /sdk-starter (single README, 3 scripts: start-local, start-mock-server, smoke-test).
- Slides: 12 slides max; 5 live demo steps; 1 common troubleshooting slide.
- Lab helpers: 2 on-call engineers for first-day, Slack channel #sdk-bootcamp-live.
- Telemetry check: dashboard template with a single panel for latency, error-rate, token-cost-per-call.

Quickstart flow (90-minute path):
0) 0–10 min: intros + goals + account/token check.
1) 10–25 min: repo checkout + install + run devcontainer.
2) 25–45 min: run sample app, call hosted API generate endpoint, inspect response, annotate prompt.
3) 45–60 min: add a second route for embeddings, index a small doc, run similarity search.
4) 60–75 min: swap config to local sidecar proxy, trigger a forced rate-limit to see fallback path.
5) 75–85 min: enable telemetry and validate events appear in dashboard.
6) 85–90 min: wrap-up, next steps, feedback link.

Minimal CLI commands to include in README (one-liners participants can paste):
- git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk-starter.git && cd sdk-starter
- ./scripts/start-local.sh (spins up mock server + sample app)
- ./scripts/run-smoke.sh (runs 5 quick API calls, prints tokens, latency)
- ./scripts/switch-sidecar.sh (flip endpoint to local proxy)

Telemetry & observability:
- Events to capture: request_id, route, model, prompt_hash, tokens_sent, tokens_received, latency_ms, fallback_taken (boolean).
- Minimal instrumentation: 1 trace per user action, error level mapping, and a single histogram for token-cost-per-request.
- Lightweight dashboard: latency (p95), error-rate (5m), tokens-per-call average, fallback-rate.

Engineering constraints and guardrails for the starter repo: 
- No heavy dependencies; prefer 40MB total install size.
- Single-file config override for tokens/env (ENV_FILE=.env.local).
- Mock mode must run entirely offline (no calls to hosted infra).
- CI smoke run that exercises 3 endpoints and fails if p95 latency > 2s (used as gate for merges).

Open questions / decisions to resolve (action owners noted):
- Should quickstart use the hosted sandbox token or local emulator by default? (Owner: Priya — decision due 2025-11-22)
- Rate-limit scenario: provide deterministic failure versus random throttling? deterministic favored for reproducibility. (Owner: Liam)
- UX: single monorepo or language-specific starters? tradeoff: maintenance vs clarity for new devs. (Owner: Maya)

Common gotchas and troubleshooting notes (copyable into README):
- If mock server fails on start: run ./scripts/clean-volumes.sh and retry; Docker sometimes leaves dangling mounts on macOS.
- Token refused: ensure ENV_FILE is loaded and token has sandbox scope; show how to exchange short-lived token via /internal/token-ops.
- Telemetry missing: confirm local SDK instrumenter is enabled (ENV REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=1) then run the smoke script.

Post-bootcamp follow-ups (automations):
- Auto-send repo + short video (5–7 min) to participants 1 hour after session.
- Trigger a follow-up survey link and collect reproducibility flags.
- Create a follow-up JIRA for any blocker > P2 surfaced during session.

Light-weight exercises for 30–60 minute extension sessions:
- Prompt engineering lab: iterate prompt with temperature/stop tokens and measure length/quality tradeoffs.
- Cost tuning lab: switch quantized model config and observe token-cost delta on the dashboard.
- Rollout lab: configure canary percentage and validate telemetry splits.

Notes for docs team (what to convert into long-form docs):
- Single-page quickstart that mirrors the 90-minute flow with copyable snippets.
- Troubleshooting appendix with the 10 most frequent errors and fixes.
- Telemetry schema reference and minimal ingestion example.

References / links to patch in existing artifacts:
- Jira: DEVEX-1203 (bootcamp infra), DEVEX-1210 (telemetry schema), ENG-3051 (sdk-starter PR).
- GitHub: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter branch: bootcamp-2025.

Immediate next steps (this sprint):
- [Maya] finalize starter repo scripts and add deterministic throttling hook (ETA 2025-11-18).
- [Priya] draft one-page quickstart and pre-req email (ETA 2025-11-20).
- [Liam] build local dashboard template and wire minimal telemetry (ETA 2025-11-22).

Quick feedback log (from run on 2025-10-29):
- "Really loved the single-command start, but the telemetry setup was confusing." — Eng Bootcamp attendee
- "We hit a macOS Docker mount bug; add note in pre-reqs" — Solutions SE

Scratch ideas (future):
- A browser-based ephemeral playground that runs entirely in the browser with WebAssembly mocker for basic response shapes.
- A micro-certification badge script that issues a small markdown certificate if a participant completes the exercises and passes smoke tests.

Last edited by Maya Patel on 2025-11-15.
